title: Judgement Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: Judgement upright: awakening, calling, renewal; reversed: hesitation. Love, work, advice, Waite's 1911 text and the 1909 card. Draw it for your question.
image_alt: Judgement, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a winged angel in the clouds blows a trumpet hung with a white banner and red cross, while figures below rise from open tombs with arms raised.
capsule: Judgement, card XX of the Major Arcana, stands for awakening, rebirth, a calling and renewal. Reversed, self-criticism or hesitation drowns out the call. It is a hopeful card that asks for an honest review, not punishment. To a yes or no question it answers yes upright, because the trumpet sounds and the figures rise to answer it.

blocks.heading: What is on the Judgement card?
paragraphs: A great angel leans out of a bank of clouds and blows a long trumpet. Waite writes that "he blows his bannered trumpet, and the cross as usual is displayed on the banner" (p. 148). On the 1909 card the angel has golden curls and dark wings touched with red, the trumpet is gold, the banner is white with a red cross, and XX is printed at the top.

Below, figures stand up out of open tombs, arms opened or hands joined, faces turned up toward the sound. Waite places "a woman on the right, a man on the left hand, and between them their child, whose back is turned", and notes that here "there are more than three who are restored" (p. 148). On the 1909 card the tombs are long open boxes set in water, with more figures behind them and white mountains on the horizon.

Waite stresses their shared mood: the figures are "as one in the wonder, adoration and ecstacy expressed by their attitudes" (p. 148). He reads the scene as a summons that "is heard and answered from within" (p. 148).

The trumpet is the symbol he keeps returning to. He asks: "What is that within us which does sound a trumpet and all that is lower in our nature rises in response" (p. 151). He allows that, for some, the card will go on showing the Last Judgment and a bodily resurrection, but asks readers with "inward eyes" to look further (p. 151).

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about Judgement?
paragraphs: The upright list is about change: a new position, renewal, the way something turns out. Waite also records one line from a much darker account, which Arcana Diary leaves aside. The reversed list starts with weakness and timidity, then shifts to the slower work of weighing things up and deciding.

Waite thought renewal was the plain sense of the card; others say it signifies renewal, "which is obvious enough" (p. 28). He also counted it among the few trumps that, in his words, "contain the legend of the soul" (p. 316).

blocks.heading: What does Judgement mean upright?
paragraphs: Awakening comes first with Judgement: a moment when you see your own story more clearly and feel a calling toward something. That calling may be quiet, an idea that keeps coming back, or loud, a choice you can no longer set aside.

The card asks for self-reflection without harshness. Looking back here is a review, not a trial: what did I learn, what am I ready to leave, who am I becoming? Renewal grows out of honest answers to those questions. That is why the card is also read as rebirth and absolution: a fresh start that comes from forgiving yourself, and an important decision made with a clear head.
Waite's change of position fits as well: after a clear look, your place in a situation can shift. So ask what has been calling for your attention and what one honest reply to it would be.

blocks.heading: What does Judgement mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, Judgement often shows the call being drowned out. Self-criticism gets so loud that you keep replaying mistakes instead of learning from them, or hesitation leaves a needed choice waiting for a perfect moment. Sometimes it is simpler: ignoring the call because answering it would change things.

Waite's reversed list holds both sides: weakness and timidity on one hand, deliberation and decision on the other, as if the call has been heard and the answer is still being weighed. Reading it as harsh self-judgment is a modern reading, not Waite's.
Give yourself the fairness you would offer a friend, then choose one next step.

blocks.heading: What does Judgement mean in love?
paragraphs: An honest review is what Judgement can bring to a relationship: renewing a commitment, naming what has changed, or closing a chapter in peace. Any of the three can be a fair answer to what has changed in you. Judgement is also the card most often read as a second chance in love: a reconciliation, or an old bond seen with new eyes.

The same clear look works without a partner: notice what you repeat each time you meet someone, and decide what you want now rather than what you settled for before. Seeing your own patterns lets you choose with fresh eyes.
When Judgement is reversed, the look back at your romantic past may turn harsh. Forgiving yourself can be part of opening your heart again.

blocks.heading: What does Judgement mean for work and money?
paragraphs: Judgement's call at work may be a pull toward a different role, a skill you keep circling back to, or a project that finally asks for an answer. It also suits taking stock of your path so far.
Its money meaning is a reckoning: settling old accounts, an honest look at debts and spending habits, and clear decisions made after learning from past money mistakes.
A reversed Judgement asks whether fear of past errors is keeping you from acting at all.

blocks.heading: What is Judgement's advice?
paragraphs: Act on one thing you keep feeling called to do, even if the first step is only a message or a sign-up form. Answer rather than wait for a louder signal. Keep the reply small and real, and let it count.

blocks.heading: Is Judgement a yes or no card?
Judgement as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: The person Judgement shows has woken up to what matters to them and is ready to stand by it; the same awakening can be yours, the self that finally hears its call clearly. In a question about feelings, the card stands for a bond being looked at again with honest eyes: relief mixed with resolve, a renewed wish to try, a readiness to forgive and be forgiven. Reversed, those feelings get stuck in doubt, guilt or blame, and a decision about the relationship keeps being put off.

pairs.text: A chapter closes and a new call sounds. Let the ending finish before you answer.
Quiet reflection, then a clear inner call. Listen alone first, then act.
A call to leave what no longer fits. Ask what you are walking toward, not only what you are leaving.
The call turns into a spark. Give it a first concrete shape.

blocks.heading: Judgement or Temperance?
paragraphs: Both cards show an angel. In Temperance, Waite has the angel "pouring the essences of life from chalice to chalice", with one foot on earth and one on water (p. 124); today that card is read as balance and patience. The angel of Judgement does not pour; it calls, and the trumpet asks for an answer. Waite himself links them, saying Judgement "may be compared with" Temperance (p. 151). Steady blending points to Temperance; a wake-up call, to Judgement.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about Judgement
paragraphs: What keeps calling for my attention, however often I set it aside?
Am I looking at my past to learn from it, or to punish myself?
What would one honest answer to that call look like in practice?

faq.q: Is Judgement a good or bad card?
faq.a: Good, as a rule. It backs fresh starts that come out of honest thinking, and it rarely asks for more than a reply to something you already sense. Its challenge is the inner critic: going over the past helps only when it leaves room for kindness.

Both spellings name the same card. The 1909 card prints JUDGEMENT along the bottom, while Waite's book heads the chapter "The Last Judgment" (p. 148), without the middle e. Arcana Diary follows the spelling on the card.

faq.q: Does Judgement mean I am being judged?
faq.a: No. Despite the name, the card passes no verdict on you and predicts none. Waite saw the trumpet as something sounding inside a person (p. 151), and the modern reading follows him: the only review here is your own, and its purpose is to free you rather than condemn you.

Its picture follows the traditional scene its old name describes: an angel, a trumpet, a cross on the banner. Waite accepted that some will see only that scene, yet he read it as an inner event (p. 151). On Arcana Diary the card makes no religious claims; it speaks about waking up to what matters to you.

waite.quote: Change of position, renewal, outcome. Another account specifies total loss though lawsuit. Reversed: Weakness, pusillanimity, simplicity; also deliberation, decision, sentence.
